work.title: The Wheels on the Bus
work.note: The Wheels on the Bus é uma canção infantil americana, associada a Verna Hills e registrada na primeira metade do século XX. Cada estrofe descreve uma parte do ônibus e o som ou movimento que ela faz: as rodas giram, o limpador de para-brisa passa e a buzina toca. facts.sub: City buses in the USA can be a cheap way to travel, but each city has its own rules. Knowing how to ask a few questions makes your first ride easy.

compare.br: In Brazil, many people use a card at the turnstile (some lines still have a cobrador), and buses can get very full.

pages.title: Waiting for the bus in the city · 1/3
paragraphs: This morning I waited at a bus stop in the city. A man named Ethan was next to me. He looked at the sign, then he looked at me. “**Excuse me, does this bus go downtown?**” he asked.
“**Yes, it goes downtown**,” I said. “**How much is the fare?**” he asked. “**Two dollars and fifty cents**,” I answered. “**Do I pay the driver?**” “**Yes, or use a card**.”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Waiting for the bus in the city · 2/3
paragraphs: Then the bus came. It was blue and white, and it was almost empty. We got on, and Ethan put the money in the machine. “**How long does it take?**” he asked. “**About twenty minutes**,” I said.
We sat near a window. The city moved past us: buildings, trees, people with coffee. I like buses because I can look outside and think. Ethan took a small notebook and wrote the name of each street.

pages.title: Waiting for the bus in the city · 3/3
paragraphs: When we came near downtown, I pressed the stop button. A red light said “Stop requested.” Ethan stood up and said, “**Enjoy your trip!**” I smiled and said, “You too!”
I thanked the driver and got off. A simple talk at a bus stop made my morning better.

pages.title: Som e ritmo
pairs: “Does this” sai rápido, quase “duz-this”. A voz sobe no fim da pergunta.
Na pergunta, “does it” soa como “duzit”. O foco forte é em “long”.
“And” é fraco: “two dollars-n-fifty cents”. Marque “dol-”, “fif-” e “cents”.
